claim: A meta-analysis of 13 studies (551 patients) of LITT for temporal lobe epilepsy found a pooled seizure-freedom rate of 58% (95% CI 54-62%), 66% (58-74%) in mesial temporal sclerosis, not associated with ablation volume; pooled complication rate 17%.

bibliographic_record.authors: Kerezoudis P, Parisi V, Marsh WR, Kaufman TJ, Lehman VT, Worrell GA, Miller KJ, Van Gompel JJ
bibliographic_record.title: Surgical Outcomes of Laser Interstitial Thermal Therapy for Temporal Lobe Epilepsy: Systematic Review and Meta-analysis

supporting_passage: Overall seizure freedom rate was 58% (95% confidence interval [CI], 54%-62%) and was not significantly associated with total ablation volume (P = 0.42), hippocampal ablation (P = 0.67), or amygdala ablation (P = 0.33).
passage_location: Abstract, Results section. Abstract only (full text not read). Europe PMC REST API (resultType=core, abstractText) for PMID 32750511; https://europepmc.org/abstract/MED/32750511; accessed 2026-11-01

population_and_design.design: systematic review and random-effects meta-analysis of observational studies
population_and_design.population: temporal lobe epilepsy treated with LITT

endpoint.reported_endpoint: seizure freedom rate (definition/class not specified in abstract)

reported_observation: Pooled seizure freedom 58% (TLE) and 66% (MTS); no significant association with ablation volume.
author_inference: Evidence insufficient to support a relationship between seizure freedom and total, hippocampal or amygdala ablation volume.
contradictions: Wu 2019 (Bayesian location model, n=234) found ablation location/amygdalar volume associated with Engel I; Kerezoudis meta-regression at study level found no volume association (ecological vs patient-level analysis).
overlap_note: Pools published LITT cohorts (likely includes Gross 2018 Emory series; to_verify). Shares underlying patients with other LITT meta-analyses in this family; do not count as independent.
